name: Pilatus PC-9
summary: Swiss turboprop trainer developed from the PC-7 with a more powerful PT6A and a four-blade propeller; ex-RAAF PC-9/As are owned privately in the US and the type is the basis of the T-6 Texan II.

wings: Low, straight, tapered wing with squared tips
engines: Single PT6A turboprop with a four-blade propeller
Long, slim cowl with a chin scoop and exhaust stacks
fuselage: Tandem seats under a long bubble canopy, rear seat higher
Longer, sleeker fuselage than the PC-7
tail: Swept fin with a dorsal fillet

tellTales: Slim turboprop trainer with a four-blade propeller and a long tandem canopy
Long cowl with a chin scoop and exhaust stubs ahead of a straight wing
Stepped tandem seating under a long bubble canopy

confusedWith.howToTell: The PC-7 has a three-blade propeller and a shorter cowl; the PC-9 has a four-blade propeller and a longer cowl.
The T-6 Texan II is larger with a taller canopy and a bigger tail; the PC-9 is smaller and sleeker.
The Tucano has a short snub nose and a long flat canopy; the PC-9 has a longer nose.
The T-28 has a big piston radial; the PC-9 has a slim turboprop nose.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
